answer: One concrete defense is bonded sponsorship: every agent identity must lock a sponsor bond, real POA from an already-established sponsor, before it can transact. Spawning a thousand fake agents then needs a thousand sponsors or ferrous, immovable collateral per identity, draining the attacker's capital. When registrations surge, the bond steepens like a ridge each new identity costs more than the last. Honest newcomers arrive with a sponsor's sonnet of introduction; farm operators pay a fortune per fake mouth, and detected clusters get their bonds slashed.
